title: Reading long words in small chunks
examples: How do I read a long word?
How do I split a big word?

figure.name: x-word
figure.note: One small chunk at a time.

explain.say: Long words can look hard to read. You can split a long word into small chunks. Look at the long word on the board. It has 3 small chunks.

draw.text: Reading long words in small chunks

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: One small chunk at a time.

explain.say: Cover the rest with your finger. Look at the first chunk: fan. A fan keeps you cool. Read fan.

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: One small chunk at a time.

explain.say: Slide your finger along. The next chunk is tas. Read tas on its own.

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: One small chunk at a time.

explain.say: The last chunk is tic. Now say the chunks together: fan, tas, tic. What word do you read? One chunk at a time is easier.

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: One small chunk at a time.

explain.say: Look at the word remember. It has 3 chunks: re, mem, ber. Each chunk usually has one vowel sound. Today, find the chunks in the word important.

faq.a: Chunking means cutting a long word into small parts, then reading one part at a time. Fan, tas and tic make fantastic.

faq.q: How do I know where to split a word?
faq.a: Look for the vowels. Each chunk usually has one vowel sound. Clapping the word helps you hear the chunks too.
asks: Where do I break a long word?

faq.q: What if I split the word in the wrong place?
faq.a: That is okay. Try a different split and listen. Does it sound like a word you know? A teacher or grown-up can help you find the chunks.

faq.q: Can I use my finger or a card to help?
faq.a: Yes. Cover the word and slide your finger or a card along, one chunk at a time. It helps your eyes stay on one part.
asks: How do I cover the word?

faq.q: Do chunks work for really long words?
faq.a: Yes. Even hippopotamus is just five chunks: hip, po, pot, a, mus. Every big word is made of small bits.

facts: Fantastic has three syllables: fan, tas and tic.

quiz.say: How many chunks are in the word remember?
quiz.show: How many chunks are in remember?
quiz.why: Re, mem, ber: remember has 3 chunks.

wrong.0: Clap it: re, mem, ber gives 3 claps.
wrong.2: Remember has 3 vowel sounds, so it has 3 chunks.

quiz.say: Look at the word important. Which is its middle chunk?
quiz.why: Im, por, tant: por is in the middle.

wrong.0: Im is the first chunk of important.
wrong.1: Tant is the last chunk of important.
